name: Dick Cheney
role: US Vice President (2001-2009), Defense Secretary (1989-1993), Wyoming congressman (1979-1989)
summary: Cheney was a hawkish, conservative Republican who favoured tax cuts, a strong military, expanded presidential power and domestic oil, gas and coal development. He drove the Iraq war and the post-9/11 detention, interrogation and surveillance programs, which he defended to the end. He was pro-life and anti-gun-control, but said marriage law should be left to the states and supported same-sex unions; late in life he broke with Trump and endorsed Kamala Harris in 2024.

sources.usedFor: Summary of the 2009 speech: would repeat post-9/11 steps; rejects 'punishable offenses' framing

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: In the 2004 debate he argued against raising the top income tax bracket, saying it would hit small businesses, and said he and Bush would make the tax cuts permanent; in 2000 he backed across-the-board tax relief.

surveillance-ok.rationale: He supported the NSA warrantless surveillance program and defended the Patriot Act in the 2004 debate; in 2001 he said intelligence agencies should be able to use 'any means at our disposal'.

strong-leader.rationale: He worked to expand presidential power and championed the unitary executive view; he also repeatedly stressed working across the aisle, so the evidence on bypassing gridlock is mixed.

limit-guns.rationale: In the House he opposed gun control more strongly than the NRA did, and as vice president signed an amicus brief backing the challengers in D.C. v. Heller.

empower-police-military.rationale: He voted for nearly all weapons systems in the House, promised in 2000 to rebuild the military with more resources, and backed record defense increases as vice president.

decide-locally.rationale: He pressed for local control of schools (2000) and for leaving marriage law to the states, but also supported national testing under No Child Left Behind and strong federal executive power.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In 2000, 2004 and again in 2009 he said people should be free to enter any union and that marriage is a state matter; Wikipedia reports he came to publicly support same-sex marriage after leaving office. He did not push for a federal rule.

abortion-legal.rationale: In 2000 he said he and Bush were 'clearly both pro-life'; in the House he opposed abortion and federal funding even in cases of rape or incest.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He ridiculed Kerry's 'global test' and UN-approval requirement for using force (2004) and said inspections gave false comfort (2002), but also said Iran sanctions should go through the UN Security Council.

limit-growth.rationale: In 2000 he said the US must not accept a false choice between energy development and the environment and warned that lacking energy supply could shut down the economy.

democracy-best.rationale: He called elected democracies the only guarantee against terror and a task of his generation (2004); he did not address voters choosing badly.

military-superiority.rationale: He argued in 2000 that the US must rebuild its military so adversaries are deterred and 'fear us', and co-wrote a book arguing the world needs a powerful America.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He cited budget deficits for his 1980s votes against new programs and favoured a balanced-budget amendment; in office he backed tax cuts alongside deficit reduction pledges, so the record is mixed.

force-without-un.rationale: In 2004 he criticised Kerry's view that troops should not deploy preemptively without UN or 'global test' approval, and defended the Iraq invasion as exactly right.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He promoted Wyoming oil and coal in Congress and in 2000 called for developing domestic energy supplies including drilling in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.

national-mission.rationale: In 2004 he said that after removing hostile regimes, the US must 'stand up democracies' in their place and called this the task of his generation.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: In 2009 he rejected moves to treat Bush-era detainee and interrogation policy as 'punishable offenses' and defended the policies as legal.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He cited Martin Luther King's 'content of their character' standard and said freedom means freedom for everybody (2000).

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He said terrorism requires 'extraordinary measures' and defended detention and harsh interrogation as legal under presidential war powers; he did not state a general view on suspending legal protections.

head-commands-forces.rationale: He called the commander-in-chief role the most important presidential responsibility (2000) and held that the president controls the executive branch; the statement's ministers clause is not addressed directly.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred: he held that NATO should remain the foundation of European security and argued for US leadership abroad, which is contrary to ending alliances.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred: as Defense Secretary he held NATO should remain the foundation of European security, and in 2019 he questioned Trump's commitment to NATO; he is not quoted on an attack-on-one-is-attack-on-all principle.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: In 2000 he proposed letting younger workers invest part (2%) of their payroll tax in personal retirement accounts; this was a partial rather than complete replacement.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: As a congressman he strongly backed aid to the Nicaraguan contras; the statement is general and this is one recorded instance.

non-intervention.rationale: He drove the Afghanistan and Iraq interventions and the Bush Doctrine that regimes harbouring terrorists are hostile; in 2004 he said he would recommend the Iraq invasion again.

public-access-to-information.rationale: He resisted disclosure of energy task force documents and invoked executive privilege against congressional requests; contested, he never argued against a right of access in general.

defeat-communism.rationale: He backed Reagan, voted for nearly all weapons systems and aid to the contras in the 1980s, and later described weapons systems as crucial to winning the Cold War.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: he argued for rebuilding and strengthening the military and said its purpose is to fight and win wars.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: he backed Reagan's confrontation of the Soviet bloc and NATO as the foundation of European security.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He argued the US should not wait to be attacked and defended preemptive war in Iraq in 2002 and 2004 ('exactly the right thing to do').

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: In the House in the 1980s he favoured a constitutional amendment to balance the budget.

equal-conscription.rationale: He opposed the Equal Rights Amendment in the House and said in 2000 he would back it only if women would not be drafted, so he wanted women exempt from the draft.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: In 2000 he said racial progress was real but the country still had a long way to go, citing profiling, education and income gaps; he did not address the specific claim.

notes: Views changed on Head Start, the Education Department and the Martin Luther King holiday (he later reversed or said he would no longer oppose). His memoir In My Time (2011), Exceptional (2015) and the May 2009 AEI speech full text could not be fetched; the interrogation position rests on quoted excerpts. No answer was found for torture-specific, Iraq-WMD-specific or Trump-specific statements because none of the 490 statements addresses them directly.
